name: Ho Chi Minh City
provinceNote: A centrally run city. Since 1 July 2025 it includes the former Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu and Bình Dương. The walkable center is still the old core.
summary: Southern Vietnam’s busy main city, the former Saigon, full of landmarks, markets, museums and street food. See the cathedral, the post office and the Reunification Palace, learn the war’s history at the War Remnants Museum, shop at Ben Thanh Market, and eat com tam and banh mi. Good for city lovers and as a base for Cu Chi and the Mekong Delta.
fee: Check on arrival. Palace and museum prices do not match across the pages that print them.
getThere: Tân Sơn Nhất is 7 km from the centre. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Ho Chi Minh City — the square, the palace, and what to eat
seoDescription: Nguyễn Huệ, the cathedral square, the Reunification Palace, and the War Remnants Museum. Area figures disagree. Tân Sơn Nhất is 7 km from the centre.
intro: Many residents still say Sài Gòn. Visit HCMC says the city’s history is a little more than 300 years, and that the old name is still in daily use. The walkable center on the visitor pages is the old core, even after the 2025 merger. Nguyễn Huệ runs from City Hall, which is not open to the public, down toward Bạch Đằng, and Vietnam Tourism says it is liveliest at sundown. The cathedral stands at the head of Đồng Khởi, with the post office opposite.

Eat cơm tấm and hủ tiếu. Vietnam Tourism says phở is best in Hanoi and that hủ tiếu is the bowl that belongs here. The Reunification Palace and the War Remnants Museum are the war record. Their ticket pages do not match the older 15,000 đồng line. Chợ Lớn is a half-day inside this city, at Bình Tây and Thiên Hậu, not a separate place.
gettingAround: Tân Sơn Nhất is the airport. Vietnam Tourism says it is just 7 km from the centre, with taxis, ride-hailing, and city buses. Check on arrival.

Metro Line 1 is running. The project page and the December 2024 opening article put the line from Bến Thành to Bến xe Suối Tiên, about 19.7 km, 14 stations, with a 29-minute ride in that opening article and an initial clock of 05:00–22:00. Visit HCMC instead names Bến xe Miền Đông as the eastern end. Both stay. The 2024 fares, 6,000–20,000 đồng a ride and the day and month passes in that article, are not a 2026 price. The fare now is Check on arrival. The same visitor page names the Saigon Waterbus, public bicycles, and more than 150 bus routes, with no fare. It says to cross with a slow, steady pace, and it prints rush hours of 7:00–9:00 and 16:30–18:30.

stayAreas.name: Đồng Khởi and Nguyễn Huệ
stayAreas.summary: A room within a walk of Đồng Khởi and Nguyễn Huệ is the center the visitor pages describe. Bùi Viện is the other night, where it crosses Phạm Ngũ Lão, Đề Thám, and Đỗ Quang Đẩu. Hotel brands named on the welcome page are not picks.

eat: Cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, bánh mì, bánh xèo, gỏi cuốn, and cà phê sữa đá are the plates with a photograph of the dish. Vietnam Tourism says this city mixes regions, and that phở is best in Hanoi.
The food guide is the streets, the doors those pages name, and the three fine-dining rooms. A stall price is not printed there.
interestsBody: The southern table, the cathedral square, the war record, Chợ Lớn, and the Ben Thanh hall. Sidewalk coffee is a glass, not a lake.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Cơm tấm is the plate Vietnam Tourism calls essential here. Hủ tiếu is the bowl Vietnam Tourism says is best in this city.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, the snail streets, and the three fine-dining rooms the national page names.

interestGroups.title: Dong Khoi and the cathedral square
interestGroups.summary: The twin-spired cathedral at the head of Đồng Khởi, the post office opposite, the opera along the street, and Nguyễn Huệ at sundown.

cards.title: Notre-Dame Cathedral
cards.summary: Both towers and the rose window. The interior hour is Check on arrival. The post office is the building opposite.

cards.title: Central Post Office
cards.summary: The hall opposite the cathedral. Two pages do not name the same architect.

cards.title: Opera House
cards.summary: The facade on Đồng Khởi. A night show is a separate ticket. No daytime interior hour was printed.

cards.title: Nguyen Hue
cards.summary: The walking street from City Hall to Bạch Đằng. Vietnam Tourism says it is liveliest at sundown.

interestGroups.title: The war record
interestGroups.summary: The palace on Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa and the museum on Võ Văn Tần. Their prices do not match the older 15,000 đồng line.

blocks.heading: The palace and the museum
paragraphs: The palace ticket page, applied from 1 August 2025, prints palace-only at 40,000 đồng for an adult and a palace-plus-exhibition ticket at 80,000. The homepage prints adult 80,000. Vietnam Tourism’s attractions page prints 15,000 đồng. All three stay.

The museum’s own terms, applied from 1 October 2026, print 60,000 đồng for an adult. The same attractions page prints 15,000 đồng. Pupils and students on the museum page are a free online ticket, not the half-price row.

cards.title: Reunification Palace
cards.summary: The halls on the old Norodom site, and the basement command center. Read the ticket page and the homepage together.

cards.title: War Remnants Museum
cards.summary: Three floors of artifacts and photographs, and aircraft in the courtyard. The operator’s adult price from 1 October 2026 is 60,000 đồng.

interestGroups.title: Cho Lon
interestGroups.summary: The Chinese neighborhood Vietnam Tourism tells you to walk. Bình Tây and Thiên Hậu are the halls. Chợ Lớn stays an area of this city.

cards.title: Binh Tay Market
cards.summary: The wholesale hall in Chợ Lớn. The gate carries the clock and the name. Bến Thành’s hours do not apply.

cards.title: Thien Hau Temple
cards.summary: The hall of Thiên Hậu in Chợ Lớn. Visit HCMC dates the building to 1760.

interestGroups.title: Ben Thanh and the halls
interestGroups.summary: Bến Thành faces Quách Thị Trang. The aisle photograph is souvenirs. Vincom Center is the mall Visit HCMC names with the walking streets.

cards.title: Ben Thanh Market
cards.summary: The clock tower and the name, on the square where the metro station sits. The food stalls are at the end of the hall.

cards.title: Vincom Center Dong Khoi
cards.summary: Named by Visit HCMC with Saigon Centre–Takashimaya. The photograph shows the Lê Thánh Tôn and Đồng Khởi signs. A street number was not printed.

interestGroups.title: Sidewalk coffee
interestGroups.summary: Cà phê sữa đá in the park outside the palace, and the sidewalk glass Visit HCMC names at Turtle Lake. The photograph is the glass, not the lake.

cards.title: Cà phê sữa đá
cards.summary: The Saturday morning cup outside the palace, and cloth-filter coffee on the welcome page. No recipe was printed.

faqs.q: Is Ho Chi Minh City the same as Saigon?
faqs.a: Visit HCMC says the city is still widely called Sài Gòn. Ho Chi Minh City is the official name. Since 1 July 2025, Resolution 202/2025/QH15 joins the former city with Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu and Bình Dương. The center you walk is the old core.

The resolution prints 6,772.59 km² and 14,002,598 people. An April 2025 proposal printed 6,772.65 km² and 13,706,632 people. A feast-streets page says nearly 9 million. All three stay. No single coordinate was printed, so there is no map pin.

Cơm tấm, which Vietnam Tourism calls the go-to breakfast and also an any-meal plate. Bánh mì starts a morning on the city itinerary. Cà phê sữa đá is the Saturday cup in the park outside the palace. Chợ Tân Định is the Sunday morning market on Hai Bà Trưng, in District 3 on that itinerary.

season.label: Drier from December to April
season.note: Vietnam Tourism says December to April is drier, sunny, and less humid, and May to November brings short afternoon showers. It is hot all year.
